overview: Server-side anticheats treat this clientbound packet as plumbing: the server pushes a full NBT compound onto a tracked entity, and no movement or combat check keys off it. The corpus shows three anticheats that register or rewrite it (Intave rewrites the entity id inside it, Artemis maps it into its packet library, Negativity lists it in its packet registry) plus Grim's NBT validation logic, which targets client-sent item NBT in the opposite direction. The packet itself carries no client-controlled data, so there is nothing to flag.

checks.name: NBT book exploit validation (ExploitB)
checks.purpose: Validates the NBT attached to client-sent book items and flags compounds the client could not have produced legitimately. The only NBT-content check in the corpus.
checks.how_it_works: Listens for item-slot and book-editing packets, diffs the new book compound against the old one the anticheat tracks, and flags with literal codes: BOOK_NO_NBT when a signed book carries no compound, BOOK_MODIFIED_NBT when unrelated tags change, plus too-many-pages and page-length counters. It faces the client-to-server direction; the S49 server push is never validated because the server authored it.
checks.detects: NBT-fabrication exploits on written books, including the classic command-block NBT injection via book tags that older clients allowed.
checks.variations: Intave registers UPDATE_ENTITY_NBT in PacketId and feeds it to EntityReader, and Artemis maps PacketPlayOutUpdateEntityNBT to PacketPlayServerUpdateMetadata in HardcodeMap; neither validates NBT content. Only Grim parses compounds, and it does so on the inbound item path.

checks.name: Entity id translation filter (EntityIdFilter)
checks.purpose: Rewrites entity ids in serverbound and clientbound entity packets so Intave tracks entities under its own local id scheme. UPDATE_ENTITY_NBT sits in the outbound rewrite list.
checks.how_it_works: A ProtocolLib filter with two subscriptions: inbound USE_ENTITY, ATTACK_ENTITY and ENTITY_NBT_QUERY packets get their local id translated to the global id, and the outbound list (which includes UPDATE_ENTITY_NBT) maps every entity id back to the local id through ConnectionMetadata, minting new local ids on first sight. It reads the first integer field of each packet, never the NBT payload.
checks.detects: Not a cheat check. It is an id-translation layer that keeps killaura, reach and position checks consistent with the anticheat's own entity table.
checks.variations: Artemis and Negativity only register the packet name in their packet libraries; neither filters or reads it. Grim's PacketWorldReaderEighteen reads NBT on chunk and tile-entity data, which is a different wire path from the entity NBT push.
